facts.text: Broad Run takes its name from the waterway that winds through the village, giving the town its identity.
Chapman's Mill, also known as Beverley’s Mill, sits two‑thirds of a mile east‑southeast of town center and was the site of the Civil War Battle of Thoroughfare Gap.
The Broad Run/Little Georgetown Rural Historic District spans nearly 9,500 acres across Fauquier and Prince William counties, preserving a rare 19th‑century agricultural landscape.
When railroads fell out of favor, Broad Run’s bustling late‑19th‑century community dwindled, leaving fewer than five historic homes and scattered stone foundations.
The Broad Run postal area’s southern edge once housed the historic town of New Baltimore, now largely outside the modern postal boundaries.
Today, Sharkawi Farms spices and Meriwether Vineyard’s Pearmund Cellars Winery showcase Broad Run’s ongoing agricultural charm.
